title: AegisBid Omega
subtitle: Technical implementation, issue resolution and measured validation

rows: Authenticated HTTP contracts, strict UUID/integer-cent validation, authorization and independent request lookup. Pure ASGI security middleware and Linux uvloop reduce dispatch overhead.
Individual bid ingress grouped into bounded internal RPCs; shared prepared-frame fanout. Current scale layout separates admission and live services; its capacity regression remains open.
Sole decision authority: durable intake, ordered transactions, leases, offers, final allocation and hash ledger. Bounded per-process connection pools.
File-backed command journal; stable message IDs, explicit consumer ACK and retryable relay. SQL reconciliation recovers missing/unpublished commands.
Bidder, seller, administrator and auditor views; same-origin routing, countdown, reconnect, pending UUID persistence, private history and winners.
Chained canonical events, optionally signed export manifests, independent replay and authenticated encrypted offsite artifacts.
Scheduled logical-artifact backup, alternate-path restore; pg_dump/exported snapshots, pg_basebackup, WAL archiving and PITR.
Local services and isolated drills; CloudNativePG synchronous replicas, NATS TLS/quorum, zone placement, Barman resources and EKS templates.
SQL/gateway telemetry, dashboards, controlled chaos, 39 backend tests, Go race checks and GitHub Actions. ReportLab/python-docx generate this report.

blocks.text: 1.1 Authority and response semantics

A browser submits only request_id and amount_cents; the server derives bidder identity from its session. A globally unique UUID binds one immutable bidder/auction/amount tuple. 202 QUEUED follows SQL commit; it proves durable intake, not acceptance, stock allocation or a JetStream quorum ACK. 200 ACCEPTED / REJECTED / CLOSED is a terminal result. Reusing a UUID with changed payload returns 409; capacity/rate exhaustion returns 429. An uncertain transport acknowledgment requires retrying the same UUID.

The admission transaction also creates a command publication receipt. Relay publishes with Nats-Msg-Id=request_id and records acknowledgment separately. Workers read the SQL queue in intake order, including requests whose broker publication is missing. Decision batches commit their business states and audit records together; notifications occur afterward. Go polls authenticated SQL-backed snapshots; it currently does not consume live outbox subjects. Redis is not required for this authority model.
1.2 Deployment and evidence baseline

Measured HTTP proofs used six API processes, one decision worker, one relay, one Go ingress and five generators on a shared 12-CPU / 7.46-GiB Docker VM. The current branch adds separate Go admission/live services and a two-second scale fanout tick. Two historical HTTP runs passed 50k; later configurations regressed. Current combined-live capacity and repeatability are unproven; phase 13 remains unmerged. Page 7 identifies the actual runs. Payment collection and fulfillment are outside the implementation.
Source: aegis/api.py, auth.py, db.py, pipeline.py; services/realtime/gateway/; apps/web/app/page.js; infra/compose*.yaml; scripts/render_ha.py.

blocks.text: 3.2 Parallel admission without overtaking

Admission takes globally sorted request-UUID transaction advisory locks, preventing conflicting reuse across auctions. A short per-auction reservation lock allocates sequence ranges and orders intake-lock acquisition. Ordinary inserts hold a shared transaction intake lock and can run in parallel. The processed watermark provides a fast capacity check; near the 60,000-pending bound, exclusive intake locking permits an exact queued count. SQL stamps eligibility; rollback/retry may leave sequence gaps, but committed decision order remains increasing.

The prefix barrier prevents an uncommitted lower sequence from being overtaken. Releasing it before evaluation lets later admission inserts continue; the auction row lock still serializes decision batches. A new worker boot gets a distinct holder. An expired lease advances the epoch; a live competing holder or stale expected epoch is fenced. Crash-before-commit rolls the batch back. Crash-after-commit/redelivery finds terminal states and unique decisions, preserving one business effect per UUID.
3.3 Price, stock and deadline rules

required = max(reserve, high + increment) if high else reserve
eligible interval = [opens_at, closes_at) using SQL admitted_at
winners = top stock distinct offers by amount DESC, sequence ASC

BIGINT cents avoid floating-point money errors. Same-price competitors cannot both advance the global high. An accepted bidder can later be displaced from stock; ACCEPTED is not a winning allocation. Close waits until eligible queued requests drain, then ranks distinct current offers and seals the close event atomically. Administrative close updates the deadline under the intake/auction locks.

Closed-auction bug and fix: earlier intake could create QUEUED rows after final close while workers scanned OPEN auctions. Admission now writes terminal CLOSED plus reason/time for a new late UUID. It leaves sealed events, winners and anchor unchanged; earlier UUID retries retain their original result. Reconciliation repairs legacy stranded rows. Source: infra/postgres/001_core.sql, 002_parallel_intake.sql; aegis/engine.py, engine_batch.py, rules.py.

pages.title: Bottlenecks, implemented changes and API behavior

headers: How it was tackled / verification boundary
rows: A global Go cache mutex previously covered upstream network calls. Network verification now runs outside it; per-token flights coalesce identical sessions and a 256-slot bound permits distinct sessions concurrently. Go race/concurrency checks cover this behavior.

Pure ASGI middleware, Linux uvloop, grouped identity lookup (2 ms), direct admission grouping (100 ms), and Go groups up to 512 requests / 100 ms with eight in-flight RPCs per auction. Every item still verifies a real JWT and bidder role.
Intake held the hot auction row

SQL sequence reservation plus shared intake locks allow parallel inserts. The worker exclusive prefix barrier preserves earlier committed ordering; sorted UUID locks preserve conflict semantics. PostgreSQL rollback, capacity and ordering tests cover these invariants.
Relay contended with queued business rows
command_queue holds publication ACK metadata. Relay no longer updates the same queued request rows locked by the decision worker; the compatibility timestamp is synchronized only for terminal rows.
Up to 512 individual decisions/events commit together, with one latest-version outbox row. All per-bid histories and hashes remain independently stored; signed replay checks the full sequence.
Fault restart also reran schema DDL

Logs showed migration DDL deadlocking with admissions after Compose restarted dependencies. The harness now starts only the recorded worker container and requires an unchanged migration start timestamp. This fixes test isolation, not the remaining throughput regression.

Separate Go services, larger live heap allowance and a two-second scale snapshot tick were attempted. Later HTTP and combined runs still failed their cutoff gate; a complete root cause or reliable capacity improvement is not established.

blocks.text: 4.1 HTTP and live-update contracts

POST /v1/auctions/{id}/bids accepts a UUID and strict integer cents (1..10^12). Go bounds the body to 1,024 bytes, forbids extra fields, validates origin/session presence and forwards only server-read cookies. The hidden /internal/v1/admissions endpoint requires a separate service key before parsing; FastAPI verifies each JWT, current role and quota. GET /v1/bid-requests/{id} and /v1/me/bids resolve private outcomes. GET auction/winners reads authoritative projections; a WebSocket snapshot never decides acceptance.

Go shares prepared frames; each client has one replaceable pending snapshot slot. The default tick is one second; current scale profiles use two seconds. Reads are limited to 1,024 bytes with 60-second pong renewal; writers use five-second deadlines and 20-second pings. Three source failures force reconciliation. Defaults cap sockets at 60,000 total/per auction and ten per user; production uses 25,000 per gateway. DB pools use 1..16 connections per process/DSN with five-second acquisition/connect timeouts. These are configured bounds, not capacity guarantees.

5.1 Identity and service boundaries

Passwords use salted scrypt (N=16,384, r=8, p=1). Four-hour HS256 sessions require subject, issuer aegisbid and expiry. Cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Secure in production. The server loads the authenticated identity and role; public bid bodies cannot choose bidder_id. Owner/admin checks protect private histories and receipts. PUBLIC_ORIGIN validates browser writes behind TLS proxies. Admission service keys use constant-time comparison and are independent of session-signing secrets.

Gateway session-to-subject caching lasts up to 30 seconds for socket admission; each bid still undergoes FastAPI token and role verification. Rate/connection limits are process-local; fleet-wide enforcement, IAM/MFA and full account lifecycle remain production work. Application pods receive no S3 backup credentials. Production manifests configure PostgreSQL CA verification, TLS NATS clients/routes, read-only filesystems, dropped capabilities, disabled automatic service-account token mounts and default-deny network policies.
5.2 Auction Black Box / BidDNA: chain and independent replay

H_0 = 64 zero characters
H_i = SHA256(ASCII(H_(i-1)) || canonical_JSON(event_i))
canonical_JSON = sorted keys + compact separators + ASCII escaping
bidder pseudonym = SHA256(string UUID)
signature = Ed25519(canonical unsigned export manifest)

Each bid event records request UUID, pseudonymous bidder, integer amount, SQL admission time, intake order, decision sequence, status and reason. A repeatable-read export fixes rules, ordered events, winners, version and terminal anchor. AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY enables manifest signing. A private bid receipt references its event/hash; it is not a separate signature or payment credential. UUID pseudonyms do not prevent the operator retaining an identity mapping.

The independent verifier does not call the engine price evaluator. It checks contiguous event sequence, hash predecessors/digests, duplicate requests, eligibility, price progression, distinct current offers, stock bounds, allocation order, close placement, exported version and stored winners. Changed winners, missing/reordered events or payload tampering fail. Unsigned evidence is INCOMPLETE. A signed export requires an independently trusted public key: an adjacent downloaded key alone does not establish provenance, and an original malicious signer is outside this guarantee. SQL administration can alter tables; the ledger is tamper-evident relative to trusted evidence, not WORM storage.
5.3 Telemetry and controlled failures

rows: SQL decision totals, recent decisions/s, queue/outbox depth, lease epochs and admission-to-recorded-decision p50/p95/p99. Row timestamps are not exact transaction visibility measurements.
Per-process connected clients/hubs, snapshots, auth failures and slow-writer disconnects; production needs full replica discovery and aggregation. Provisioned Grafana panels visualize those signals.

Requires development/test and ENABLE_CHAOS=true; admin-only pause/resume and fixed faults. API has no Docker socket/arbitrary command field. The local controller restart-gateway/disconnect-client actions currently restart the API service; a dedicated Go fault is not implied.
backup_jobs and recovery_runs retain checksums, statuses, checkpoint metadata, verification results and measured recovery scope. Process/job success alone does not prove business correctness.

pages.title: HA, backup transport and verified restoration

blocks.text: 6.1 Primary loss, broker quorum and zone placement

CloudNativePG 1.30.1 configures three PostgreSQL instances with ANY 1 synchronous standby acknowledgment, required durability, failover quorum and isolation checks. The operator controls promotion/read-write routing; application lease epochs cannot fence independently writable database primaries. NATS uses three file-backed replicas with authenticated TLS and verified routes. One broker replica can fail while publishing remains available; loss of a safe majority must not produce a false durable ACK. SQL reconciliation retains unfinished business work.

PostgreSQL/NATS require zone anti-affinity; stateless workloads spread across zones, with gateway autoscaling from three to twelve replicas and a 600-second scale-down window. EKS templates define three subnet pairs, per-zone NAT, private workers, encrypted disks, KMS-protected secrets, audit logs and EBS CSI identity. Templates/operator resources were validated; EKS was not launched. The actual kind primary-node stop/promotion drill used simulated zone labels and a small dataset; it is not a physical whole-zone or 50k-load database-failover proof.
6.2 Why the recovery layers are separate

rows: pg_export_snapshot and pg_dump -Fc share a repeatable-read checkpoint. Manifest captures counts, sequence positions and SHA-256 file hashes; artifact corruption is checked before import.

Director schedules jobs; File Daemon reads prepared staging; Storage Daemon writes media; PostgreSQL Catalog indexes jobs/files. Restore selects an alternate directory, then imports into a fresh database. Catalog/configuration and encryption keys also need independent protection.

pg_basebackup with SHA-256 manifest and pg_verifybackup; continuous WAL archive; named/time recovery target with recovery.signal. WAL publication uses temporary copy, fsync and atomic hard-link; an existing segment must compare identically.

Client AES-256-GCM binds the object key as associated data; encrypted index is published last. Restore downloads exact VersionIds, authenticates/decrypts artifacts and verifies the database. Newer corrupt indexes cannot replace a pinned valid version.

Reject a populated destination; import only into an isolated database/project/volume. Check manifest/counts/sequence positions, independently replay ledger/winners and issue a JSON/HTML recovery certificate. Promotion to authority remains an operator decision.

blocks.text: 6.3 What was actually verified

Bacula backup and restore jobs completed with T status; an isolated restored dataset contained 20 decisions, 21 events and three winners. Physical PITR recovered a decision absent from the base backup and matched the ledger anchor. A real private Singapore S3 round trip verified server-side encryption, client encryption, version-pinned restore, 30-day COMPLIANCE retention and protected-version deletion denial. The remote bucket uses the configured account; independent backup-account administration was not demonstrated.

Production remote continuous WAL is configured through Barman Cloud plugin 0.16.0, an ObjectStore, WAL-archiver patch and scheduled physical backups. These resources are not an end-to-end production offsite PITR/RPO proof. archive_timeout=60s is not a site-loss RPO guarantee. Recovery timers on page 7 cover controlled small-dataset import/retrieval/verification intervals; they exclude full-site reconstruction. Source: scripts/backup_export.py, scripts/rehearse_pitr.py, infra/bacula/, infra/pitr/, infra/offsite/, infra/ha/; docs/recovery.md, ha-deployment.md.

Current status: historical normal and worker-failure HTTP runs passed the 50,000-user gate. Later layouts regressed; the branch is not certified for repeatable 50k or combined-live operation and phase 13 remains unmerged. All original failed trials remain FAIL. The 30-request / 7.96-bids/s smoke test is retained as historical data, not the assignment-scale proof.

No successful-run request remained queued at final close. Recorded cutoff ACCEPTED/REJECTED/QUEUED counts: normal 2,260/17,708/30,032; historical worker 3,198/6,530/40,272. HTTP ingress p50/p95/p99: normal 0.369/1.108/1.515 s; historical worker 0.326/0.734/0.853 s. Winning integer-cent totals were 10,196,980 and 10,196,880 respectively. All four rows passed their recorded audit/correctness gate; the latest missed the bidding-window gate.
7.1 Workload, failure and correctness evidence

One hot auction used stock 20, reserve 10,000 cents and increment 10 cents; amount_i=10000+10i for i=0..49999. Five generators seeded 50,000 distinct users and pre-issued real HS256 sessions. Each offered one original bid over nine seconds inside the final ten-second window (about 5,556 offers/s). HTTP transport pooled at most 5,120 connections, not 50,000 simultaneous transactions. All services/generators shared one 12-CPU / 7.46-GiB Docker host; login and multi-host capacity were not measured. PostgreSQL fsync, synchronous_commit and full_page_writes stayed on.

Both historical passes checked all 50,000 SQL histories and matched all original client CSV requests to 50,000 signed bid events plus one close event and 20 replayed winners. Owner HTTP histories and same-UUID retries were sampled for 64 users. Tampered winners failed; a new late UUID returned CLOSED without changing the sealed anchor. The worker trial confirmed SIGKILL/exit 137, checkpoint preservation and epoch 1 to 2 with stale-holder fencing. Earlier Compose restart could also rerun migrations; the corrected harness restarts only the worker and checks migration start time. Current combined trials held 50,000 distinct sockets but failed bidding cutoff.

SQL admitted_at is stamped inside the admission transaction; HTTP ACK follows commit. Decision committed_at is also an in-transaction row timestamp, not the exact WAL-flush/MVCC-visibility instant. Cutoff counts are reconstructed from those times; saved roughly one-second SQL samples record committed observations separately. Eligible queued work drains after cutoff. Successful admission does not imply every decision completed inside ten seconds.

Exact runs, image IDs and full commands are in docs/bidding-proof.md and docs/evidence/bidding-index.json. Offline check: python -m scripts.verify_bid_stress docs/evidence/bids-<full-run-id>. Rebuild PDFs with python -m scripts.build_report and python -m scripts.build_demo_guide. Checks: 39 backend tests, Go race tests, frontend build and phase CI; later report edits require only document validation. Source baseline f607529 produced the historical passes; 9474f91 is the current benchmark-code checkpoint.

Remaining: repeatable current-layout 50k bidding, combined-live throughput, physical multi-zone deployment/outage, independent-account backups, continuous production offsite PITR/RPO, predictive fleet pre-warming, fleet-wide quotas, payment settlement and a real legacy benchmark. The demo uses small live requests plus labelled recorded capacity/recovery evidence; full-load runs, cloud provisioning and live-database restores stay outside the three-minute presentation.
